comparator.name: Theology (Theologie)
comparator.academicYear: Adopted 2026–27 OER for the full-time standard 180-EC route, rechecked 2026-10-13; current public prospective pages also consulted
comparator.route: Ordinary full-time 180-EC Theology bachelor, first-listed 15-EC thematic module and 30 EC free space
comparator.sourceNotes: The target is Radboud bachelor Theology CROHO 56109 with full-time and part-time delivery; this coherent 180-EC reconstruction uses the ordinary full-time academic sequence, not the 120-EC shortened route, part-time pacing or 180-EC Theology master. The 2026–27 adopted OER identifies 150 EC major (135 EC required major units plus one 15-EC required thematic module) and 30 EC genuinely free minor space. Its Appendix II identifies 60 EC required in year one, including 5 EC Liturgiewetenschap, biblical Hebrew, biblical interpretation, fundamental theology, pastoral theology, dogmatics and religious inquiry. The public year-one page displays only 55 positive EC while claiming 60 and omits Liturgiewetenschap; the applicable adopted OER supplies the missing compulsory unit. Year two has 60 EC required in theology, Christian history, ethics, Greek, New Testament exegesis, church law, spirituality and the 10-EC methods/research project. Year three comprises 5 EC humanities practice, one selected 15-EC required thematic module, 30 EC genuinely free minor space and a 10-EC independent theology final work. The first-listed module Worldviews, Nature and Climate is selected neutrally; its three 5-EC components are identified by the OER. Other module options and the optional teacher minor are not added. Public pages use descriptive names for some units, while the OER supplies their formal 2026–27 status and credits.

routeSelection.route: Ordinary full-time 180-EC Theology bachelor, first-listed 15-EC thematic module and 30 EC free space
routeSelection.basis: The target is the ordinary Theology bachelor, not the separate shortened programme or master. The adopted OER allows a choice of one required thematic module in year three; the first-listed Worldviews, Nature and Climate module is selected independently of UCR fit. The 30-EC genuinely free space remains unspecified; full-time pacing is used to display the coherent 60+60+60 academic route.

core: Belief, meaning, Christian thought and questions about the good life
Christian history, biblical interpretation, texts and religious traditions
Practical theology, lived faith, spirituality and care
Religion in contemporary society: secularisation, institutions, equality, freedom and justice
Historical, philosophical, literary, sociological and empirical research methods
adjacent: Worldviews, climate, nature and environmental responsibility
questions: What gives life meaning, and what constitutes a good life?
How should religious traditions and public institutions respond to diversity, justice and contemporary social problems?

alternatives.label: Worldviews, meaning & public life
alternatives.concept: Study questions of belief, meaning and the good life through philosophy, myth, literature, history, archaeology and visual heritage, then examine religious diversity, rights, institutions and political conflict through sociology, psychology, law and politics. This related-fields route does not provide Christian theology, biblical Hebrew or Greek, scriptural exegesis, liturgy or pastoral formation.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum gives sustained weight to philosophy and cultural interpretation together with law, sociology and politics. Its label describes those related fields and does not imply a Theology degree.
progression: Introductory philosophy, sociology, politics, archaeology and law precede advanced constitutional, social-theory, conflict, heritage and interpretive work. Law, Society & Justice precedes Comparative Constitutional Law. All courses use exact planned terms; seven are at 300 level.

alternatives.label: Ethics, worldviews & environmental responsibility
alternatives.labelReason: Ethics and political philosophy are integrated with a sustained sustainability, climate, ecology, governance and technology sequence, so the label states both the normative and environmental centres.
alternatives.concept: Examine what humans owe to nature, future generations and one another through ethics, political philosophy, worldviews and environmental justice, grounded in climate science, ecosystems, circularity, sustainability governance and renewable-system design. This route responds to the programme’s formal Worldviews, Climate and Nature direction without presenting environmental philosophy as Christian theology.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the first route, this programme replaces twelve courses in literature, heritage, psychology, constitutional law and conflict with a sequenced environmental curriculum in climate, sustainability systems, life-cycle analysis, ecosystems, remediation, renewable design, governance and delta research. Each programme therefore has 90 EC not present in the other, above the 30-EC floor.
progression: Sustainability Essentials I precedes Sustainability Essentials II, which precedes advanced remediation and renewable-system work. Introductory philosophy and climate science precede applied ethics, political philosophy, sustainability governance and advanced environmental courses. All formal prerequisites and exact planned offerings pass; eight courses are at 300 level.

candidates.label: Religion, care & spiritual practice
candidates.assessment: UCR can study health psychology, ethics and the social organisation of care, but it has no theology, pastoral formation, spirituality sequence or supervised spiritual-care practice. A third programme would therefore turn general health and ethics courses into substitutes for a specifically religious-care direction.

selection.assessment: The historical judgment correctly identified the absence of Christian theology, biblical languages and exegesis, but it applied a full-substitution threshold. UCR can construct one coherent route in worldviews, meaning and public life and a second, substantively different route around the programme’s formal Worldviews, Climate and Nature direction. Religion and care is the next coherent generator-backed direction, but UCR lacks theology, pastoral formation and spiritual-care practice, so production stops at two.

blocks: The selected comparator module studies worldviews, climate and nature from a theology-and-religion perspective. The UCR route addresses environmental ethics, science and governance but not theology.
Both develop research design, but UCR Qualitative Research Methodology is not theology-specific.
The comparator requires an independent theology thesis; UCR optional research can support an independent project but does not supply theological supervision or methods.

notes.text: Radboud Theology is a Christian-theology degree with biblical Hebrew and Greek, Old and New Testament exegesis, doctrine, liturgy, pastoral theology, church history and law, spirituality and an independent theology thesis. UCR can study worldviews, meaning, ethics, cultural heritage, religion in public life and environmental responsibility through adjacent humanities, social sciences and sustainability fields, but neither route reproduces the theological discipline.

UCR offers no biblical languages, sustained scriptural exegesis, systematic or pastoral theology, liturgical studies, canon law or supervised spiritual-care practice. Philosophy, literature, history, law and sociology courses remain related perspectives and are not represented as substitutes for those missing components.
